scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_adjustment.purpose: Posts an adjustment to a customer's overall A/R balance — not to a specific invoice — such as a goodwill credit, a correction of a mis-billed utility charge, an approved write-off of a small balance, or a debit to re-bill a missed charge.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_adjustment.outcome: The customer's balance is corrected with a documented reason and the offset posted to the right revenue, concession or bad-debt account.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_adjustment.rootCause: Resident and commercial tenant balances drift from what is actually owed because of billing errors, disputed charges and negotiated settlements. Adjustments let the balance be corrected without falsifying the original invoices, and they must be controlled because they are a common way to hide skimmed cash (crediting a paid resident's account to cover a diverted payment).
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_adjustment.ifSkipped: Resident ledgers show incorrect balances, collections chase amounts that are not owed, and uncontrolled credits can conceal misappropriated receipts.
gaap: ASC 606-10-32 — price concessions as variable consideration for non-lease charges
redFlags: Credits issued by site staff who also receive payments
Large or frequent adjustments without documentation
Adjustments coded to revenue accounts rather than concessions or bad debt

scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_invoice.purpose: Creates a receivable invoice to a customer who is billed outside the resident rent cycle — commercial tenants, affiliated entities, laundry or cell-tower licensees, or cost recoveries such as utility and expense bill-backs.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_invoice.outcome: Amounts owed to the property are recorded as receivables and revenue or cost recovery in the correct period.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_invoice.rootCause: Not all property revenue flows through OneSite resident billing. Commercial space, ancillary contracts and recoveries from affiliates must be billed and tracked, or the property loses revenue and cost recoveries go uncollected.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_invoice.ifSkipped: Revenue is understated, cost recoveries are never collected, and receivables from affiliates are not tracked.
gaap: ASC 842-30 — lease income for commercial tenants
redFlags: Bill-backs that do not tie to the underlying expense invoices
Invoices to affiliates never settled

scr_ar_close_a_r_subledger_page.purpose: Closes A/R summaries for a period so no one posts A/R invoices, payments or adjustments into that period after month-end.
scr_ar_close_a_r_subledger_page.outcome: The A/R aging at period end is fixed and agrees with the 1210 balance in reported financials.
scr_ar_close_a_r_subledger_page.rootCause: Late payments and adjustments are routinely dated into prior periods. Closing the subledger keeps reported receivables and revenue stable after reporting.
scr_ar_close_a_r_subledger_page.ifSkipped: Reported A/R and revenue change after reporting, and the aging no longer ties to the balance sheet.
redFlags: A/R subledger open after GL close
Summaries reopened without approval

scr_ar_customer_aging_report.purpose: Shows receivables by customer aged by due date (current, 30, 60, 90+), used to manage collections, estimate bad debt and reconcile to the A/R control account.
scr_ar_customer_aging_report.outcome: A collection priority list and the basis for the allowance for doubtful accounts, reconciled to 1210.
scr_ar_customer_aging_report.rootCause: Delinquency is a leading indicator of revenue loss. Aging drives collections, eviction decisions and the bad-debt reserve, and must tie to the GL.
scr_ar_customer_aging_report.ifSkipped: Collections are not prioritized, bad debt is under-reserved, and A/R subledger differences go undetected.
gaap: ASC 326 — expected credit losses for non-lease receivables
redFlags: Aging total not tying to 1210
Prepaid (credit) balances not reclassed to 2120 Prepaid Rent
Former residents with balances not sent to collections

scr_ar_delinquency_report.purpose: The curated workflow for tracking past-due resident balances aged 30, 60 and 90+ days to calculate bad-debt reserves, drive collection and eviction actions, and write off uncollectible former-resident balances.
scr_ar_delinquency_report.outcome: Delinquency is actively managed, the allowance reflects expected losses, and uncollectible balances are written off on schedule.
scr_ar_delinquency_report.rootCause: Rent delinquency directly reduces NOI. Asset managers track delinquency and bad debt as key performance metrics, and GAAP requires recognizing lease income only when collection is probable.
scr_ar_delinquency_report.ifSkipped: Uncollectible rent stays in revenue, A/R is overstated, and bad debt appears in large lumps when finally written off.
gaap: ASC 842-30-25-12 — lessor income limited to cash received when collectibility is not probable
redFlags: Balances over 90 days with no reserve
Write-offs not sent to collections
Delinquency concentrated in units with repeated payment plans

scr_ar_gpr_tieout.purpose: The curated workflow for reconciling the rent roll to the GL revenue accounts: gross potential rent, loss/gain to lease, vacancy, concessions and employee units, so reported rental revenue matches what the property actually billed and should have billed.
scr_ar_gpr_tieout.outcome: A monthly GPR tie-out that proves revenue in the GL is complete and correctly split among GPR and its contra accounts.
scr_ar_gpr_tieout.rootCause: Institutional owners report revenue on a GPR basis (GPR less vacancy, concessions, loss to lease and bad debt) to analyze performance. The GPR posting is often a manual JE from rent roll data, so a tie-out is needed to prove it matches the rent roll.
scr_ar_gpr_tieout.ifSkipped: Revenue components are misstated, occupancy and loss-to-lease analysis is wrong, and asset managers draw wrong conclusions about pricing and occupancy.
redFlags: GPR per GL differs from rent roll market rent
Vacancy loss inconsistent with occupancy percentage
Model and employee units not separately tracked

scr_ar_intercompany_bill_backs.purpose: Configures and uses intercompany bill-backs, where one entity pays shared costs (payroll, insurance, utilities) and bills them back to related entities, automatically creating receivables and payables between them.
scr_ar_intercompany_bill_backs.outcome: Shared costs are recovered from the entities that incurred them, with matching Due To and Due From balances.
scr_ar_intercompany_bill_backs.rootCause: Shared-service structures mean one entity often pays for others. Billing back correctly ensures each property's P&L carries its costs and affiliated balances are settled.
scr_ar_intercompany_bill_backs.ifSkipped: Costs stay on the paying entity, affiliate balances do not reconcile, and owners are over- or under-charged.
redFlags: Billbacks not tying to source invoices
Affiliate balances aging without settlement

scr_ar_receiving_a_payment.purpose: Records a payment from a customer and applies it to specific open invoices, starting from the invoice record, the A/R invoice list or the payment screen.
scr_ar_receiving_a_payment.outcome: Customer balances and A/R are reduced, cash is recorded (often to Undeposited Funds), and payment history is traceable to invoices.
scr_ar_receiving_a_payment.rootCause: Correct application of payments to invoices matters for aging accuracy, late-fee assessment and dispute resolution. Misapplied payments create false delinquencies and credits.
scr_ar_receiving_a_payment.ifSkipped: A/R and cash are misstated, customers are dunned for paid balances, and late fees are charged incorrectly.
gaap: ASC 310 / ASC 842 — receivable reduction on collection
redFlags: Payments applied to the oldest balance when the customer specified an invoice
Unapplied payments left on account

scr_ar_recurring_invoices_list.purpose: Automates repeating customer invoices — commercial rent, ancillary licenses, monthly affiliate charges — so they generate on schedule.
scr_ar_recurring_invoices_list.outcome: Predictable billing with consistent revenue recognition and fewer missed charges.
scr_ar_recurring_invoices_list.rootCause: Manual monthly billing leads to missed invoices and lost revenue. Automation ensures charges are billed consistently, but the list must be maintained when agreements change.
scr_ar_recurring_invoices_list.ifSkipped: Charges are missed or continue after agreements end.
gaap: ASC 606 / ASC 842 — revenue recognized as earned
redFlags: Recurring invoices for expired agreements
Escalations not applied

scr_ar_reversing_payments.purpose: Reverses a posted customer payment — applied to the wrong customer or date, or returned NSF — reinstating the invoices it paid; reversals cannot be undone, only corrected with a new payment.
scr_ar_reversing_payments.outcome: Customer balances and cash reflect reality after payment errors or bounced payments.
scr_ar_reversing_payments.rootCause: Payments get misapplied, and resident payments bounce. Reversal is the controlled way to reinstate the balance and, for NSF, to trigger NSF fees and collection.
scr_ar_reversing_payments.ifSkipped: Balances remain wrong, NSF payments stay credited, and cash is overstated.
redFlags: Reversals without bank evidence of NSF
Reversal dated in a reconciled period
